sections.heading: C — Avoiding Crashes
sections.markdown:
## C — Avoiding Crashes

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A94
Braking, steering and acceleration are the manual’s three possible ways to avoid a collision or lessen its impact. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A94
Antilock brakes help maintain steering control during a stop. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A94
Read the vehicle owner’s manual for instructions on using its antilock braking system. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A94
An ABS pedal can vibrate and the system can make a clicking sound during operation. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A94
For a vehicle without ABS, consult its owner’s manual for the appropriate braking method. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A94
If a collision cannot be avoided by stopping in time, steering around the hazard may provide an escape. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A94
When steering around a hazard, avoid braking during the turn if possible, particularly when entering a soft shoulder. [A94]
Source: [A94 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A95
For a quick steering response, hold opposite sides of the wheel at 9 and 3 or 8 and 4. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A95
After steering clear of an obstacle, countersteer toward the original lane and remain ready for another correction. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A95
Grip the wheel with both hands when making an emergency steering maneuver. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A95
Choose an escape direction that avoids other traffic, then straighten and reduce speed after clearing the hazard. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A95
A swerve can lead to a second collision, so watch the escape path as well as the initial obstacle. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A95
Acceleration may sometimes avoid a vehicle about to strike from the side or rear. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A95
For that acceleration escape, a manual-transmission vehicle may need a downshift; the automatic-transmission example uses the accelerator. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A95
Reading printed material while driving is prohibited, with a map and written directions to a particular destination excluded from that definition. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A95
If a rear impact is imminent, be prepared to brake so the vehicle is not pushed into one ahead. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A95
If a side impact spins the vehicle, be ready to steer to try to regain control. [A95]
Source: [A95 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A96
After a crash, stop immediately, assist injured people as possible and arrange an ambulance when needed. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A96
Do not move an injured person unless another danger requires moving them to safety. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A96
The manual directs involved drivers to remain at the crash scene until police arrive and question those involved. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A96
Move the crashed vehicle out of the traffic path if you can do so. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A96
Collect names and addresses for everyone involved, injured people and witnesses. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A96
Record the other driver’s name, address and license number, checking that the name matches the license. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A96
Record the other vehicle’s make, model, year and plate number, its damage and the insurance company’s name. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A96
Document when and where the crash occurred and the vehicles’ and pedestrians’ positions and travel directions before and after it. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A96
Record poor weather or road conditions relevant to the crash. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A96
Contact police for a crash involving injury and give factual information about the event. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A96
If you damage a parked vehicle, try to locate its owner; if unsuccessful, leave a note where the owner can find it. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A96
The parked-vehicle note should identify you by name, address, driver-license number and plate, and give the crash date, time and damage description. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A96
The pinned manual requires a report to police or the local sheriff for any crash injury or property damage of at least $2,000. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A96
Failing to report a reportable crash can lead to criminal charges and suspension of the driver’s license. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A96
For an otherwise nonreportable crash injuring or killing a dog, cat or livestock, take reasonable steps to notify the owner or, if unavailable, law enforcement or animal control. [A96]
Source: [A96 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A97
When emergency medical responders are already at a crash, follow their instructions and keep attention on the road and traffic officers. [A97]
Source: [A97 -> pdf-0097]

Misconceptions: emergency avoidance can involve steering or acceleration as well as braking. [A94]
Mnemonic: observe, choose an escape, maintain control, seek help.
Glossary: ABS means antilock braking system. [A94]
Dynamic facts: contradictory braking instructions, medical techniques and equipment procedures require verification.

sections.heading: C2 — Avoiding Crashes
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Avoiding Crashes

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A97
If you encounter an injury crash with no one else present, try to help the victims. [A97]
Source: [A97 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A97
Stay away from fallen electrical wires and let emergency personnel handle them. [A97]
Source: [A97 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A97
When wires touch or lie near a crashed vehicle, warn its occupants to remain inside until help arrives. [A97]
Source: [A97 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A97
A skid occurs when tire grip is lost, which can follow excessive speed or overly hard braking. [A97]
Source: [A97 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A97
If skidding begins, ease pressure on the brake or accelerator and look toward the desired path. [A97]
Source: [A97 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A97
If wheels leave the pavement, remain calm, slow gradually and hold the wheel firmly. [A97]
Source: [A97 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A98
For right wheels that have run onto the shoulder, ease off the accelerator and use gentle rather than sudden heavy braking. [A98] [A97]
Source: [A98 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A98
After slowing for a shoulder departure, check traffic ahead and behind before steering back onto the pavement. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A98
Use the maintenance schedule in the owner’s manual to reduce the likelihood of breakdowns. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A98
For brake failure while moving, the manual first directs several rapid, firm pumps of the brake pedal. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A98
If the brake-failure pumping attempt fails, apply the parking brake gradually and be ready to release it if a skid develops. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec09-R12 | anchor: A98
During brake failure, shift to a lower gear, look for a stopping place and warn others with lights and horn. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec09-R13 | anchor: A98
Once stopped after brake failure, get assistance and do not resume driving without functioning brakes. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec09-R14 | anchor: A98
Test the brakes after passing through deep water because they may pull sideways or fail to operate. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec09-R15 | anchor: A98
The manual describes drying wet brakes by moving slowly and applying light brake pressure briefly over a short distance. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec09-R16 | anchor: A98
A front-tire blowout can pull toward that tire; a rear blowout can also cause shaking or wobbling. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec09-R17 | anchor: A98
With a flat or blown tire, keep a firm grip, steer straight and avoid slamming the brakes. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec09-R18 | anchor: A98
Release the accelerator and let a vehicle with a blown tire slow gradually; brake gently only when necessary. [A98]
Source: [A98 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec09-R19 | anchor: A99
After a tire failure, pull to a safe place off the road and switch on emergency flashers. [A99] [A98]
Source: [A99 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec09-R20 | anchor: A99
For an accelerator stuck with uncontrolled speed, keep watching the road and shift into neutral. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec09-R21 | anchor: A99
With a stuck accelerator, steer smoothly, brake gently and seek a safe place off the road. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec09-R22 | anchor: A99
Turn off the engine as the stuck-accelerator vehicle comes to a stop; if the pedal cannot be freed reliably, get help and do not drive it. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec09-R23 | anchor: A99
For a breakdown, move away from traffic and make the disabled vehicle visible with emergency flashers. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec09-R24 | anchor: A99
The breakdown instructions call for warning other road users and contacting police. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec09-R25 | anchor: A99
The section-nine breakdown example places emergency flares 200 to 300 feet behind the vehicle to give approaching drivers time to react. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec09-R26 | anchor: A99
If a train is approaching and a stalled vehicle cannot be moved from the tracks, stop trying to move it and escape. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec09-R27 | anchor: A99
To escape debris from that rail collision, move away from the tracks at 45 degrees toward the approaching train. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec09-R28 | anchor: A99
Once safely clear of the tracks, use the railroad emergency telephone number shown on the nearby blue sign. [A99]
Source: [A99 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec09-R29 | anchor: A100
For an oncoming vehicle in your lane, use the horn and flash the lights to warn its driver. [A100] [A99]
Source: [A100 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec09-R30 | anchor: A100
For that head-on threat, brake promptly while avoiding wheel lock, and escape to the right shoulder or ditch rather than the left lane. [A100] [A99]
Source: [A100 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec09-R31 | anchor: A100
Do not smoke while jump-starting a vehicle, and protect your eyes. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec09-R32 | anchor: A100
For a vehicle entering water, the manual identifies a window as the preferred exit because water pressure can obstruct a door. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec09-R33 | anchor: A100
Open powered windows promptly if a vehicle enters water because its electrical system may fail. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> pdf-0100]

sections.heading: D — Avoiding Crashes
sections.markdown:
## D — Avoiding Crashes
Accuracy scope: Avoiding Crashes facts use the pinned official PDF with a registered primary page and any explicitly declared supporting pages; original phrasing preserves actor qualifications, exceptions and modal verbs.
Physical94 simultaneously instructs sustained ABS pressure and quick pumping; routine non-ABS pumping and controlled-braking superlatives also need equipment clarification. Those conflicting techniques are withheld. [A94]
Bodily bracing, steering-wheel grasp for side impact, face shielding and throwing an unbelted body across the seat are held for contemporary restraint/airbag review. [A95]
CPR/rescue-breathing qualification, victim-dragging technique, limb elevation, burn cooling and shock measures require clinical review before learner instruction; no detailed medical protocol is exported. [A97]
The crash-report threshold and scene-wait directions are pinned manual statements, not a current legal signoff. [A96]
The categorical brake-warning-light statement and engine-off-while-moving brake-failure step need equipment-specific clarification; the latter is withheld. [A98]
Flooded-engine starting, generic jumper-cable connection order and floating-time claims lack vehicle/current safety context and are withheld. [A99] [A100]
Rail escape direction is explicit prose; this does not establish any universal debris-free trajectory. The flare range remains a source-specific example rather than an exclusive legal minimum. [A99]
Confidence process: every drafted fact received a same-model source-context check before submission; independent coverage and hallucination QA remain pending.
Officeholders, telephone numbers and changing administrative details are excluded from stable learner statements. No source attribution is a legal or clinical signoff.
